issue.title: [VNET] VLAN sub interface RIFs are not assigned to VNET

failure.body:
**Description**

VLAN sub interfaces are not attached to VNET and appear in the global routing table.

**Steps to reproduce the issue:**
1. Load the following two configurations:
```json
{
        "VXLAN_TUNNEL": {
                "tunnel_v4": {
                        "src_ip": "<IP>"
                }
        },
        "VNET": {
                "Vnet210": {
                        "vxlan_tunnel": "tunnel_v4",
                        "vni": "210",
                        "peer_list": ""
                },
                "Vnet215": {
                        "vxlan_tunnel": "tunnel_v4",
                        "vni": "215",
                        "peer_list": ""
                },
               "Vnet800": {
                        "vxlan_tunnel": "tunnel_v4",
                        "vni": "800",
                        "peer_list": ""
                },
               "Vnet900": {
                        "vxlan_tunnel": "tunnel_v4",
                        "vni": "900",
                        "peer_list": ""
                }
        },
        "VLAN_SUB_INTERFACE": {
                     "Ethernet124.210": {
                       "vnet_name": "Vnet210"
                },
                     "Ethernet124.215": {
                       "vnet_name": "Vnet215"
                }
        }
}
```

```json
{
        "VLAN_SUB_INTERFACE": {
                "Ethernet124.210|<IP>/24": {},
                "Ethernet124.215|<IP>/24": {}
        }
}
```

**Describe the results you received:**

The RIFs are not attached to VNET and show in global routing table:
```sh
root@ptr-orion-t2:~/vnet/vnet_sub_eth# show ip int
Interface        Master    IPv4 address/mask    Admin/Oper    BGP Neighbor    Neighbor IP
---------------  --------  -------------------  ------------  --------------  -------------
Ethernet124.210            <IP>/24      up/up         N/A             N/A
Ethernet124.215            <IP>/24      up/up         N/A             N/A
```

```sh
root@ptr-orion-t2:~/vnet/vnet_sub_eth# show ip r
Codes: K - kernel route, C - connected, S - static, R - RIP,
       O - OSPF, I - IS-IS, B - BGP, E - EIGRP, N - NHRP,
       T - Table, v - VNC, V - VNC-Direct, A - Babel, D - SHARP,
       F - PBR, f - OpenFabric,
       > - selected route, * - FIB route, q - queued route, r - rejected route

K>* <IP>/0 [0/202] via <IP>, eth0, <IPV6>
C>* <IP>/32 is directly connected, Loopback0, <IPV6>
B>* <IP>/32 [20/0] via <IP>, PortChannel1, <IPV6>
  *                    via <IP>, PortChannel2, <IPV6>
  *                    via <IP>, PortChannel3, <IPV6>
  *                    via <IP>, PortChannel4, <IPV6>
B>* <IP>/32 [20/0] via <IP>, PortChannel1, <IPV6>
  *                    via <IP>, PortChannel2, <IPV6>
  *                    via <IP>, PortChannel3, <IPV6>
  *                    via <IP>, PortChannel4, <IPV6>
C>* <IP>/31 is directly connected, PortChannel1, <IPV6>
C>* <IP>/31 is directly connected, PortChannel2, <IPV6>
C>* <IP>/31 is directly connected, PortChannel3, <IPV6>
C>* <IP>/31 is directly connected, PortChannel4, <IPV6>
C>* <IP>/16 is directly connected, eth0, <IPV6>
C>* <IP>/16 is directly connected, Vlan200, <IPV6>
B>* <IP>/16 [20/0] via <IP>, PortChannel1, <IPV6>
  *                      via <IP>, PortChannel2, <IPV6>
  *                      via <IP>, PortChannel3, <IPV6>
  *                      via <IP>, PortChannel4, <IPV6>
C>* <IP>/24 is directly connected, Ethernet124.210, <IPV6>
C>* <IP>/24 is directly connected, Ethernet124.215, <IPV6>
```

**Describe the results you expected:**
VLAN interface RIF should work with VNET the same way other RIF types.

**Additional information you deem important (e.g. issue happens only occasionally):**

resolution.title: [vstest/subintf] Add vs test to validate sub interface ingress to a vnet
resolution.description:
**What I did**
Extended the following vs tests to validate the use case of sub interface ingress linked to a vnet:
- sub port interface creation
- sub port interface add ipv4 addresses
- sub port interface admin status change
- sub port interface remove ipv4 addresses
- sub port interface removal

**Why I did it**
Add vs test to validate that https://github.com/Azure/sonic-swss/pull/1521 fixes https://github.com/Azure/sonic-buildimage/issues/4238

**How I verified it**
vs tests

**Details if related**

vnet is a special vrf with the following limitations as of the current implementation:

- For next hop object of type IP, only directly connected subnet and single next hop to an IP prefix are supported
- Directly connected subnet to a router interface is limited to IPv4 when interface is ingress linked to a vnet

vs tests are extended to vnet with the above limitations in mind.

#### Dedendancy
- [x] Contains https://github.com/Azure/sonic-swss/pull/1521
- [x] Contains https://github.com/Azure/sonic-swss/pull/1654

Incremental change to https://github.com/Azure/sonic-swss/pull/1521 base can be found at https://github.com/wendani/sonic-swss/pull/1
